title: The Commandant's Request
lead: Commandant Dain Halloran pours two glasses of something terrible and asks, as if discussing the weather, whether your fleet would be so good as to attack his fortress. He has six thousand refugees on the Line that he can't legally release, and the regulations allow exactly one exception: losing.

gm.truth: Regulation allows a commandant under enemy attack to evacuate persons in custody rather than let them fall into enemy hands. Halloran can open the Line only if the fortress is plausibly under assault by a superior force, and he's asked for a transfer four times and would give a great deal to have this decision taken out of his hands. It has to look real, because his daughter Tess is a conscript officer on the forward line, and her posting depends on his record. If he simply opens the doors, she pays for it. If he loses a battle honestly, she doesn't. The fleet has forty-one ships and one working cannon, so the attack has to be the biggest bluff in the history of the border: painted gun ports, freighters running hot to fake warship signatures, and false battle traffic. Here's the part he hasn't said: Bastion Nine is a bluff too. Half the garrison was pulled back to Vantor after the Fall, and the great guns have no shells. Only the officers know. A captain who works that out can see the whole battle for what it is, two frauds staring at each other. His deputy, Major Ilsabet Crow, is a believer and very good at her job. She isn't fooled for more than a minute, and she comes on the open channel: "Your gun ports are painted on, Captain. I've got six thousand people on that deck who've been told they're safe here, and I'd like you to explain to me why I shouldn't call Vantor." She still has the point-defense batteries, which do work, and she has a very good poker face. That conversation should be the climax.
beats: The request, up in the Commandant's Gallery, at a desk turned to face the wall. Halloran is tired, funny and completely serious. He gives the captain the fortress's watch schedule and a date, and he asks them not to thank him.

Preparing the bluff. Paint on freighters, a very confused fleet of civilians learning to fly in formation, and Ensign Pell Asante asking the captain whether they're actually going to do this. A sharp eye on the fortress's supply manifests or a word from Severa Lune might reveal how few shells have come in lately.
The word reaches the Line, as all words do. The Line Mothers start packing without being told. Now it can't be called off without a riot.

The attack. Blank shots from the fleet, thunderous silence from the great guns, and small fast fire from the point-defense batteries at a freighter full of families. It's a very dangerous kind of theater.
Major Crow on the open channel. Whoever blinks first loses. Then the docks open, or they don't.
routes: Win the theater: tactics, gunnery and deception to stage a battle that fools eight hundred conscripts, with piloting to keep the freighters out of the working batteries.
Fix it from the inside: stealth and hacking, with Halloran's codes, to spoof the batteries' targeting and find the shell count.
Talk to the guns: leadership and persuasion on an open channel, to the conscripts at the batteries, many of whom came through the Line themselves, asking them all to aim a little wide.
checks: tactics:hard to read that the great guns aren't firing, and work out why
gunnery:moderate to put the Meridian's one cannon exactly where it scares people and hurts nobody
deception:hard to fake a warship's signature with a grain freighter
hacking:very_hard to spoof the point-defense targeting from inside
persuasion:very_hard to answer Major Crow on the open channel
commerce:moderate to round up food and berths for six thousand
fights: customs_marine on the docks if the evacuation turns ugly, and hegemony_trooper with Major Crow if she decides to come in person. Halloran's orders, once given, stand most of them down.
outcomes: If it works, six thousand people walk aboard the fleet's ships, and food becomes a crisis overnight. The fleet is overwhelmed and proud, and everyone tells the story of the painted guns. Very few people ever hear the other half of the joke.

If Crow is talked around, she joins the evacuation, or holds her fire and takes the blame herself. Either way, the Hegemony has lost a very good officer. If the captain lets slip that they know about the shells, she'll want that kept quiet as much as they will.

Halloran stays at his post to take responsibility. If the captain goes back for him, he comes, grumbling, and the Hegemony has a defector with everything in his head, and his daughter is suddenly in danger. If not, he faces a court, and his last letter arrives on the Meridian.

If the bluff fails, there's real damage to some fleet ships and a lot of people to carry home, but the fortress is shaken, and Halloran has one more idea. Hegemony standing falls hard no matter how this ends. If word gets out that Bastion Nine has no shells, the whole border changes.
gm.rewards: Six thousand grateful people, a huge swing in fleet morale, some of Bastion's military stores such as a service_rifle or old_concord_medal, and Halloran's written watch schedules for the rest of the border.
